Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan

📅 23 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 32 min read (6474 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~32 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that it had to end that way, didn’t it?
  • Newcastle versus Liverpool became the Premier League’s most dramatic fixture when Kevin Keegan was manager here and, on the afternoon they flocked to the “cathedral on the hill” to pay tribute to the late, great superstar, we were treated to a contest that was in keeping with his narrative.
  • Liverpool operating with the discipline of a basketball team undoubtedly helped, and we can examine those gaping chasms soon enough, but the poignancy of seeing Matthias Jaissle looking as bereft as Keegan at Anfield 30 years ago at the final whistle was impossible to ignore.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it had to end that way, didn’t it? A last-minute goal, a sense of what might have been and a helter-skelter contest that will take days to decipher.

Newcastle versus Liverpool became the Premier League’s most dramatic fixture when Kevin Keegan was manager here and, on the afternoon they flocked to the “cathedral on the hill” to pay tribute to the late, great superstar, we were treated to a contest that was in keeping with his narrative.

Liverpool operating with the discipline of a basketball team undoubtedly helped, and we can examine those gaping chasms soon enough, but the poignancy of seeing Matthias Jaissle looking as bereft as Keegan at Anfield 30 years ago at the final whistle was impossible to ignore.

Really, the German’s first match in charge of Newcastle should have ended with three points. His team are a work in progress – rich in youthful exuberance though prone to lapses – but how they fought, ran and worked to give the locals the result they wanted.

Sources indicate that they were almost at the finish line, seconds away from beating Liverpool here for the first time since December 2015, but then Lewis Hall ran into Victor Muñoz, sending the Spanish substitute sprawling, and Stuart Attwell pointed to the penalty spot. Dominik Szoboszlai inflicted maximum damage.

Dominik Szoboszlai equalises from the spot in the 99th minute! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/0Ag9WitqHt.

According to recent reports, “I have clear thoughts,” Jaissle noted quietly, as he was asked to reflect on the day-wrecking decision. “I guess you call it a soft penalty here. If you give it, you need to give a lot during this match and a lot during the season. I don’t know if it that is good for football.”.

Here was the third time in four seasons Liverpool had scored in injury time in front of the Leazes Stand, after Darwin Núñez (2023) and Rio Ngumoha (2025), and their eighth goal beyond the 90th minute in collisions with Newcastle is a Premier League record against the same opponents.

No wonder he was stunned. Jaissle had spent idle moments in the build-up thinking about what might happen if Newcastle scored an early goal and, much to his delight, fantasy became reality in the most thrilling fashion. On this emotional afternoon, it was fitting the hosts scored first.

One of Keegan’s great early wins as Newcastle manager was in November 1993, when his team blew away Liverpool in the snow and Andy Cole scored a first-half hat-trick. His first goal that day came after five minutes and, by happy coincidence, the clock stopped at that moment for Anthony Elanga, too.

How Liverpool went from having a chance of their own to conceding 20 seconds later is something Andoni Iraola will have to address quickly, but that is what happened: Ryan Gravenberch should have shot, instead he passed and Amar Dedic intervened, his interception finding Will Osula.

In a recent development, off Osula galloped, Liverpool’s defenders looking leaden-footed as they gave pursuit, and he ushered Elanga into open space. Once he was in the clear, he was not for catching and his shot was perfectly placed beyond Alisson Becker.

An electric start! Anthony Elanga gives Newcastle the lead inside 5 minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/8DYYFJ9i6F.

It has been revealed that as Elanga was mobbed, the recriminations started. Fingers pointed at each other, Iraola spun around in dismay. Liverpool were easy to play against last season – Iraola’s Bournemouth had scored two identical goals against them on the opening day 12 months ago – and old habits die hard.

Recent findings suggest that “We should finish the play,” Iraola conceded. “We created a great chance. We are on the edge of the box and have a clear opening to shoot and we decide not to. We don’t finish it properly and then you have to give credit to Elanga, who wins the race.”.

According to recent reports, what could Liverpool offer in response? The answer before the interval was nothing, other than a shot from Florian Wirtz that was well saved by Lukas Hornicek. The first half was wretched and it was difficult to see what had changed from the final throes of Arne Slot.

It has been revealed that this, to be clear, is no criticism of Iraola, more a spotlight on players who need to step up. They did that momentarily in the second period, when Cody Gakpo equalised. He was afforded too much time by Newcastle’s defence but, still, his finish from 20 yards was super, zipping beyond Hornicek.

According to recent reports, cody Gakpo with a fine finish to equalise for Liverpool! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/cfDQWbES2v.

But parity was secured for less than two minutes before Newcastle scored a near-carbon-copy second goal, another counter-attack – this was one led by the outstanding Yoane Wissa – ending with substitute Joe Willock finding a corner of Alisson’s net. Again the inquests followed.

"Wow!"Joe Willock restores Newcastle's advantage almost instantly with an exceptional finish! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/8IKPUgqapK.

“We had the numbers to defend it better,” Iraola said. “It’s not like they caught us by surprise, but we didn’t defend it properly. We should compete for the first ball and probably make a foul, be a little more aggressive as we had the numbers to defend it.

“You don’t want to concede transitions and we’d been preparing them in the week for transitions.”.

Why they didn’t follow the proposal that had been set is something that Iraola must address, but he will be relieved that the days spent this week are not dissecting a defeat, as Wissa should have wrapped up the contest, only for Alisson to make a brilliant save to thwart the Congolese striker.

Sources indicate that those missed chances should not have mattered but in the final throes, Hall misjudged the angle Muñoz attacked him from, he got his challenge wrong and, after a pause, Attwell pointed to the spot. Given the agony Liverpool have inflicted, the outcome was as clear as black and white.

“We scored at the end, so you have a better taste,” Iraola remarked. “Before the game, we wouldn’t have signed for this result. It’s a reward. It’s only a point, but at least it’s something that’s deserved.”.

Plenty would contest his conclusion. Liverpool got away with it – and Iraola is about to find the hard work is only just beginning.

A really soft one, if you give that, they’ll be more in the future, I’m not a fan of that.

Their heads are a little down but we know we had many challenges, we’re in a huge transition phase at the moment.

It’s a brave project but I like the challenge, working with young lads, they were tired. Lewis Miley just came back from an injury but they did an amazing job and it’s just about getting adapted to the league.

The crowd here is unbelievable and the quality. Every change can be decisive and it’s something I really enjoy. We’re clear in our approach and you can adjust in the game if you plan ahead.

It has been revealed that it’s not the result you want, but scoring in the last minute gives us a better feeling. I value that the players never gave up. I’m sure we had more chances, it’s unfair they’re winning very early and overall, I think we’ve had the better chances.

Industry observers note that we were probably in the first half not finishing anything, we had a lot of balls on the edge but we needed to shoot. We don’t finish play and then they win on the counter-attack.

The players coming from the bench gave us energy and you can feel the way we want to play.

Sources indicate that overall, we played a lot in their half and had good moments and phases on the ball. The first goal was more difficult to defend, Anthony Elanga is a fast player. The second, I think we had the numbers but sometimes you have to finish the play and try and win the ball.

What a special club, what a special man, that’s why we gave him a major credit. The fans were unbelievable today. I think we gave them so much back today and that’s what we need to give them all season.

Industry observers note that we know we needed to give the fans something after this period so that’s why we tried to start fast. The fans pushed us until the end.

It was my best [performance for Newcastle] so far. Fresh manager, new role. I’m so pleased to be here. I hope today I indicated I’m really happy.

According to recent reports, it’s rough, especially 30 seconds before the end of the game, but that’s a huge step for us. That’s the mentality we need to have through the season. The manager came three weeks ago and gave us a lot of information. Now we show on the pitch we are ready for the season. We needed this win to make a statement but in the end we draw. We have so much to work on.

It has been revealed that to be honest, I didn’t even hear the referee’s whistle. I had to look at him if I can go. I was practising a lot during the pre-season. We didn’t have any penalties during games, but in training. We need to take the positivity of the first game and move on.

Sources indicate that more than 50,000 fans in the stadium against you. You can’t hear your own voice. That’s why I love football and that’s why I am doing it.

To come here is always tough. Everybody knows the [Newcastle] fans are unbelievable. They have a great team and a manager - newly introduced but he has proven himself in many other clubs. But we were prepared and we needed to be closer to each other under a new manager as well. We needed to know what was going on in the game. It’s a good thing coming back into the game after 2-1 down.

Recent findings suggest that if I am honest, we should have won. But that’s football. You don’t win easy in the Premier League - doesn’t matter who you play against. We have to be aware of that and we need to take care in the next game.

🗣️ "It's knee on knee, it's a foul"Micah Richards and Daniel Sturridge analyse Lewis Hall's foul which led to Liverpool's late penalty. pic.twitter.com/NRw406sTcZ.

Sources indicate that 14 - Liverpool remain unbeaten on MD1 in the Premier League in each of the last 14 seasons (since 2013-14), the longest active run in the competition.Spirited. pic.twitter.com/3rluUnSBhu.

I think they did the right thing, easy to say now of course, by not giving Isak the penalty. There is enough pressure on in the 96th minute without all that would have entailed. Nor was Isak having the best of games.

Industry observers note that A familiar feeling after last season. Newcastle concede a last kick of the game penalty. Should have held on for the win. It was a soft penalty, Hall dangled out a knee rather than a leg and Munoz made sure he ran into it. But as soon as it's given on the field never going to be….

Sources indicate that the points are shared, and Lewis Hall has his hands on his knees. Jaissle protests with the officials. This was a stirring home performance from Newcastle which should build confidence for the season ahead. An irrepressible showing from Wissa was the biggest positive. Iraola will be pleased to get back on the coach with a draw after what was quite a ragged Liverpool performance, their midfield balance looked off.

What a magnificent penalty from Szoboszlai, Hornicek had no chance, and Liverpool have surely snatched a point.

Dominik Szoboszlai equalises from the spot in the 99th minute! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/0Ag9WitqHt.

Recent findings suggest that what theatre that would be... Gakpo has the ball in his hands. But no, it’s going to be Szoboszlai.

With the last kick of the game, practically. Kerkez released the ball forward, Van Dijk competed for a header, Munoz pounced on the seconds, and his pace carried enough threat to prompt Hall to step across the winger and make contact with his knee.

#NEWLIV – 90+6' The referee's call of penalty for the challenge by Hall on Muñoz was checked and confirmed by VAR. REF: "He doesn't play the ball. He makes clear contact". VAR: "It's knee into thigh contact. Confirming the on-field decision of penalty".

It has been revealed that so, so poor from Frimpong who hesitates to put a cross in, takes a couple of unconvincing touches, and then commits a foul. Mac Allister. Wissa receives a standing ovation, replaced by Schar.

In a recent development, gakpo runs down a blind alley, and it is another blunt Liverpool attack. Time running out for them now.

Liverpool corner, won by Lewis Koumas who lacked support but his cross deflects behind.

Hornicek palms away Szoboszlai’s delivery. This has been strong Premier League debut from the goalkeeper.

According to recent reports, newcastle have a throw deep in Liverpool territory after more good work from Wissa, and chaotic defending from Liverpool. Atwell has booked Gakpo for an earlier foul on Wissa.

There will be FIVE minutes of added time.

Murphy with another wonderful cross through the Liverpool six-yard box, but no player in black and white was gambling for a tap in. Liverpool just about still in with a sniff.

Cheers at St James’ Park as Thiaw ushers the ball behind as Kerkez tried to get in behind. Then Frimpong’s touch lets him down, not for the first time.

In a recent development, an aimless cross from Liverpool, and Munoz is penalised at the back post for a push. Liverpool have lacked clarity and intelligence in the last third today, but there is still time.

According to recent reports, big save by Alisson! He narrows the angle to deny Wissa the goal his performance deserves. How important could that prove to be? Liverpool have the ball again.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool with a long spell of possession in the final third, trying to tire Newcastle legs, but Frimpong’s cross is a little too high for Isak to generate any power with the header. Newcastle are just starting to sit in a touch.

Munoz runs down a blind alley, more sound defending from Lewis Hall and the Newcastle players can see the finish line now. They will be only too aware of how they lost this game in the last minute 12 months ago, though.

Szoboszlai shoots against the well, and the Araujo is booked for bundling over a Newcastle defender. Wissa thought he was away for Newcastle but the flag goes up for offside.

It has been revealed that frimpong does well to keep things alive for Liverpool, and there are half-hearted appeals for a handball penalty but Thiaw was down by his side. Another Liverpool sub: Lewis Koumas is on for Gravenberch.

The long throw is headed away, but Murphy catches Mac Allister and Liverpool have a free-kick in a crossing position. Though you never can tell with Szoboszlai around.

In a recent development, here come those changes from Newcastle: Murphy and Bamba on for Elanga and Miley. Hall’s delivery from the free-kick won by Wissa was poor.

Sources indicate that liverpool have Newcastle penned in, but Munoz’s pass is overhit and Newcastle have a goal kick. Jaissle is about to introduce Jacob Murphy from the bench. Wissa, Newcastle’s best player by a stretch, does well to win a free-kick high up the pitch from Szoboszlai.

In a recent development, araujo is on for Jacquet at the back for Liverpool, who have just threatened again. Szoboszlai hacked down but the referee waved play on, and Kerkez could not get enough curl on his cross or else Isak would have had a free header.

Willock lifts in a teasing cross from the right, Alisson palms the ball back into danger, and Ramsey cracks a shot wide of the post. Hard to say whether this game is going 3-1 or 2-2 but the scoring is surely not over.

Was that Isak’s moment? Gakpo rolls the ball back to Isak in a good shooting position just inside the box, but he slices his left-footed effort well over the bar. More cheers from the Newcastle fans.

It has been revealed that newcastle really should have three! Defence-splitting pass from Miley to release Hall, who feeds a teasing cross into the six-yard box, but Wissa could only get studs on it. Better connection and that was a goal. Liverpool so fragile at the back, though.

According to recent reports, stuart Atwell has been guessing on decisions throughout this game, and Jacob Ramsey has just been booked for what looked a clean challenge on Isak, who produced a lovely turn initially. Newcastle survive the free-kick.

Sources indicate that but then Gakpo has acres of space to run into, but Botman saves the day in the box. The game is haywire at the moment.

Here come the Liverpool changes: Ngumoha, who was the match-winner last season here, Wirtz are the players off, replaced by Munoz and Mac Allister.

Liverpool will be kicking themselves, they had Newcastle on the ropes. Iraola is preparing a triple sub. Willock was the goalscorer, but it was also a brilliant assist from Wissa.

The equaliser had been coming but that was really poor from a defensive perspective as everyone backed off Cody Gakpo and let him pick his spot.

Sources indicate that you also have to question the decision to keep Will Osula on. He was obviously struggling to move freely and it has meant Newcastle did not have an out ball.

But, just as I was going to be critical of manager Matthias Jassile one of his substitutes puts Newcastle back in front and it a brilliant goal. Magnificent build up play from Wissa, who skipped away from three Liverpool players, but it is even better from Joe Willock who takes the pass in his stride, highlights great skill t o take it on jis stride and away from Frimpong and the finish is sublime, curled into the bottom corner.

It has been revealed that jaissle can claim that as a magical substitution, but it is superb individual goal from Joe Willock. Another Newcastle counter-attack, Wissa does brilliantly to wriggle away from three players in midfield, and Willock dribbles inside Frimpong before arcing a shot into the far corner. Outstanding finish.

In a recent development, "Wow!"Joe Willock restores Newcastle's advantage almost instantly with an exceptional finish! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/8IKPUgqapK.

Jaissle with a double sub immediately after conceding: Joe Willock and Jacob Ramsey are on, replacing William Osula and Sean Steur who was a little slack on the Gakpo goal.

The game is one-way traffic, Liverpool looking to turn the screw.

The man linked with a move to Spurs all summer has equalised for Liverpool. He had a sighter a few minutes earlier, and it was too easy for Gakpo to receive the ball behind Newcastle’s midfield, and he had time to pick out the far corner with a clean hit from outside the box. Game on.

Recent findings suggest that cody Gakpo with a fine finish to equalise for Liverpool! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/cfDQWbES2v.

It has been revealed that just two touches inside the Newcastle penalty area from Isak so far, he has been subdued. Nice idea from Gakpo, chopping inside from the left, and curling a shot not far wide of the top corner.

Industry observers note that good defending from Lewis Hall up against Ngumoha, before Van Dijk passes the ball straight of play. Wissa wanted a free-kick for a challenge from behind by Gravenberch but the referee judged he touched the ball first.

Scramble at the back post from the Liverpool corner, but then a loose touch from Wirtz prompts a Newcastle break and there was a chance for Elanga to dribble into the box but he put the breaks on.

The game is already really stretched, holes appearing in Liverpool’s midfield. Wissa’s poked through ball towards Osula was just a tad overhit.

There are surely more goals to follow.

Liverpool have made a sharp start from kick off, winning a corner.

Sources indicate that just because it is a manager’s first game, we shouldn’t pull our punches. That was a scandalous first half performance from Liverpool and there is absolutely no difference in watching them now compared to what they offered through much of last season. Maybe the disappointment wasn’t about the man in the dugout. Maybe it was about the players wearing the Red shirt.

Industry observers note that 5 & 18 - 5 - Liverpool have conceded in the opening five minutes on MD1 of a Premier League season for the very first time.The Reds are winless in 18 Premier League away games when falling 1-0 behind (D6 L12) since beating Crystal Palace 2-1 in December 2023.Baptism. pic.twitter.com/K1HF2wNRVP.

Newcastle will be delighted to go in leading the game at half time but there were some worrying signs before the break.

Alexander Isak is going to be in for the sort of hostile afternoon unseen in English football for years.

Not since Michael Owen has a player left Newcastle and been so universally despised. Owen was accused of ducking out of a relegation battle to ensure he secured a lucrative free transfer move after an injury-ravaged spell in the North East.

If anything, Isak was even worse, He went on strike, refusing to play for the club again, despite having three years left on his contract, in order to force a move to Liverpool. It felt like the ultimate betrayal and crossed a line with Geordies. They will love you and worship players as good as Isak, but if you behave like the Sweden international did you become the ultimate villain.

Isak was a superb player in black and white stripes, arguably their best since the takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund in 2021. He was top goalscorer two years running and was the focal point of Eddie Hower’s attack as they qualified for the Champions League twice and won the Carabao Cup.

It has been revealed that he could have been a Geordie legend, but he left in such an ugly and acrimonious fashion. Isak forced Newcastle to buckle from their not for sale stance, rejecting a pay rise and a new contract, insisting he would never play for the club again even if they refused to sell him, that he will be tarnished forever.

In a recent development, it is sad in many ways and indicates the ugly side of the game. I’m told he does regret the manner of his exit, especially his falling out with Howe. They have not spoken since. It has weighed heavily on him since his move to Anfield.

Looks like Rio Ngumoha will play on the right flank with Cody Gakpo left, Wirtz in the No 10 role behind Isak.

There will be a powerful expression of unity between Newcastle United and Liverpool supporters in memory of their shared icon, Kevin Keegan, before this afternoon’s game.

A man who meant so much to both clubs: a phenomenal player for Liverpool and a force of nature who transformed Newcastle as both a player and a manager.

The cooperation between the two to ensure St James’ Park can deliver a special tribute to a remarkable figure in English football has been heartwarming.

Sources indicate that the sale of Curtis Jones to Inter Milan means that for the first time since Liverpool came into existence in 1892, the prospect of them going through the season without fielding a player who was born in the city for a game is real. He has also not sugar-coated anything. Jaissle knows he is up against it. Time is the enemy, given how late he arrived in pre-season and he understands the size of the task ahead.

These are early days, but the energy and purpose he has brought to the job have impressed everyone at all levels of the club. Clear communication is at the heart of everything. He explains what he expects, what he needs and what has to be done, no matter who the conversation is with.

It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Sources indicate that liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Mauricio Pochettino will never succeed as the Manchester United manager while he is forced to deal with the board's rotten decisions.

It is sad but painfully obvious to those watching United be torn apart by Liverpool in a defeat that felt so inevitable as soon as the manager's self-defeating teamsheet was revealed.

Chief executive Omar Berrada claimed recently that the back line was not a concern for the board, while insisting the team are improving and heading in the right direction.

Just over one week later, Man United have been dispatched 4-0 against their biggest rivals in a pitiful display which could have ended in an even wider scoreline.

They now have, statistically, the worst defence in Europe's top five leagues, with 34 goals conceded across all competitions so far this season.

While none of that can be placed on Pochettino's shoulders after just three training sessions, they are the same problems which have seen three previous managers sacked.

Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim, and most recently Michael Carrick, have all met the same fate under this board and they are showing no signs of changing any time soon.

Former Man United assistant manager Mick Brown told Football Insider on 16 November, shortly following Pochettino's appointment, that he is destined to fail at Old Trafford.

Rather than being an indictment on the manager, though, the concerns are with the board and the chief decision-makers who will be key to any success United have.

If Berrada and his head of recruitment Jason Wilcox genuinely believe that this squad is good enough to compete, and that they've made the right calls, they must be ousted.

The CEO speaking about the depth of options in defence, after they were forced to play two 20-year-olds in the closing stages against Aston Villa, was bizarre to begin with.

After a 4-0 defeat to Liverpool, there can be no more excuses for the board, and they have got to change their stance or risk being left behind.

Pochettino has been thrown into a nightmare situation, regardless of the allure the club still has, and will now be given an impossible job to turn their situation around.

Unfortunately, should Man United continue to struggle, the blame will fall at his feet regardless of whether he is truly at fault, while any improvements will be in spite of the board.

It is not just the fans who have been left raging at the board and the decisions made in recent weeks, as key players have also felt compelled to speak out against them.

Lisandro Martinez was the first and most vocal of them, as he directly tore into Wilcox and Berrada, questioning their transfers and suggesting they had thrown Carrick under the bus.

Football Insider revealed last month that Man United are fearing a dressing room mutiny, with large sections of the dressing room unhappy with how things are going.

Carrick ultimately paid the price for that, but after players spoke out on social media following his departure, it is clear he is not the problem as far as they are concerned.

Martinez's comments, while misjudged in the moment, echoed the feelings of the majority of Man United supporters, and Pochettino will now face the same issues.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 05:49 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 08:12 EST, 20 November 2026.

A Liverpool fan accused of racially abusing footballer Antoine Semenyo has been found not guilty after the player withdrew his support for the prosecution.

Semenyo was due to give evidence at Liverpool Magistrates' Court on Friday in the trial of Mark Mogan, 47, who was accused of shouting abuse during the opening match of the Premier League season at Anfield on August 15 last year.

But Simon Jones, prosecuting, remarked: 'Following recent contact made with Mr Semenyo, he has indicated he is no longer supportive of proceedings and the prosecution do not consider it is appropriate to compel him.

'In those circumstances we offer no further evidence in the case.' District Judge Mary Dowrick recorded a verdict of not guilty to the charge of racially aggravated behaviour.

Semenyo, who was a Bournemouth player at the time of the incident but later signed for Manchester City, had been due to give evidence last month but the trial was adjourned halfway through when Mr Mogan was taken to hospital after suffering a seizure.

The court had heard Mr Mogan, in a wheelchair, shouted at Semenyo as he went to take a throw-in about 30 minutes into the game.

Mark Mogan (right) has been found not guilty of racially abusing Antoine Semenyo (left) after the player withdrew his support for the prosecution.

He was alleged to have said: 'Hurry up and take the throw-in, you black b*****d.'.

Opening the case last month, Mr Jones remarked: 'That racial abuse was shouted directly at Antoine Semenyo, who was close to him.

'Mr Semenyo briefly froze, as he couldn't believe what the male had said.' Mr Mogan then shouted "I'm talking to you, you ****", the court heard.

Witnesses also stated they saw him throw his chewing gum at the footballer.

Semenyo reported the incident to the match referee and Mr Mogan was removed from the stadium at half-time.

Mr Mogan, who had an intermediary with him in court, told police in interview that Semenyo had called him a cripple after he shouted at the player to 'hurry up'.

Mr Mogan, of Templehill Close in Dovecot, Liverpool, declined to comment as he left court.

Semenyo, who scored a brace in the game, had brought the incident to the attention of match referee Anthony Taylor and the match was briefly halted while both managers and captains were spoken to.

At half time an announcement was made to the crowd asking for no racist abuse and pictures on social media demonstrated a man in a wheelchair being escorted along the touchline and out of the ground.

Mogan, pictured with Liverpool legend Robbie Fowler, would have been banned for life if he'd have been found guilty.

Merseyside Police later revealed the man had been arrested and then was bailed for three months pending further investigations.

Pictures on social media revealed Mogan playing wheelchair basketball for a team called the Greenbank Meteors while other images show him posing with Liverpool legends Robbie Fowler and Emile Heskey.

After he was charged, Liverpool confirmed he would be banned for life if found guilty but Judge Dowrick recorded a verdict of not guilty on Friday morning.

Industry News: Keith Wyness reveals if Bundesliga club can tempt Everton into accepting Thierno Barry offer

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (493 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Footballinsider247

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • RB Leipzig do not have the necessary financial power to tempt Everton into selling striker Thierno Barry any time soon.
  • That is according to former Toffees chief executive Keith Wyness, speaking exclusively to Football Insider, who believes that his former club have nothing to worry about when it comes to the Bundesliga interest.
  • Leipzig previously made contact over a move for Barry in the summer, and are showing a renewed interest after he has scored six goals in his opening 10 Premier League games this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

RB Leipzig do not have the necessary financial power to tempt Everton into selling striker Thierno Barry any time soon.

That is according to former Toffees chief executive Keith Wyness, speaking exclusively to Football Insider, who believes that his former club have nothing to worry about when it comes to the Bundesliga interest.

Leipzig previously made contact over a move for Barry in the summer, and are showing a renewed interest after he has scored six goals in his opening 10 Premier League games this season.

However, Wyness does not believe that the Red Bull-backed side are capable of "threatening" Everton with a lucrative offer.

Barry has become a hugely notable part of David Moyes' project this term, and he remains the only senior striker on Everton's books right now.

Wyness believes that the 24-year-old still has plenty to prove in English football, and does not expect him to depart Merseyside any time soon.

Everton’s former chief Wyness – who served as CEO at Goodison Park between 2004 and 2009 and now runs a football consultancy advising elite clubs – believes that Leipzig is the only potential move that Barry's agent may "promote" in the coming months.

However, he does not expect a switch to Germany to be something that the Frenchman gives any consideration to at all.

Speaking on the latest edition of Football Insider's Inside Track podcast, Wyness explained Everton's stance on Barry's future.

According to recent reports, "The club that I've heard have been looking, or at least his agent would be trying to promote, is Leipzig. I don't think they're going to threaten Everton in terms of the sort of money they're going to be able to offer," he remarked.

"Look, to me he's still not proven. Yes, he's got some goals. They haven't been classic striker's goals, as many know. A few have been coming in off different parts of the body.

"But listen, they're goals, and we all appreciate it, and those goals have been a big part of Everton's good start to the season.

"But yet to me he's not proven himself as a prolific striker, and it's going to take another at least until Easter, and if he's consistent and he keeps on going until Easter then we're talking about a better valuation for a player.".

Former Manchester United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider recently that Everton could yet accept a "huge" offer for Harrison Armstrong in January.

The Toffees blocked a £40million move to Nottingham Forest in the summer, but may yet take the chance to cash in and reinvest the profit into their squad.

Brown believes that Armstrong is one of few sellable assets in Moyes' squad, and also feels that they have ample cover for him in the midfield if he were to depart.

However, the homegrown ace is hugely popular among the fanbase, and it would take an eye-watering offer to tempt Everton to sell.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When building a squad it is important to have a vision of the end goal, and AC Milan have exactly that heading into 2027.

La Gazzetta dello Sport begin a report by stating that there are no transition years when it comes to Milan. Frequently they have chosen to overhaul the squad in the summer window, and sometimes even in the winter.

It has been revealed that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Sources indicate that for example, 2024 brought Paulo Fonseca with Morata, Pavlovic, Fofana, Emerson Royal, Jimenez and Abraham. Then, 2025 brought Gimenez, then Massimiliano Allegri with Modric, Rabiot, Nkunku, Jashari, and De Winter. Last summer brought Ruben Amorim with Ramos, Moreira, Gila, and Cisse.

A not-so-bold prediction: 2027 won’t be slow. Gerry Cardinale even hinted at this, stating: “We’ll continue to be aggressive and opportunistic. It will take a couple more transfer windows to complete everything.” The two transfer windows? Winter and summer, 2027.

Recent findings suggest that the Rossoneri have two key needs right now: a striker and a central defender. They’ll try to secure them as early as the month after next. Nicolo Tresoldi and Endrick are the names that have been talked about for weeks, but the transfer market has surprises.

In a recent development, the difficulties are well known: Club Brugge do not want to sell their jewel in January unless a €60m check materialises, while with Endrick it seems the will of Jose Mourinho must be taken into account. So, alternative names could emerge for the attack.

A central defender is less of a pressing need. Eight months ago, Milan decided to explore the possibility of signing Virgil van Dijk, who turned 35 in July and is regarded as one of the best of his generation.

A year ago, the conditions weren’t there, but now they might be. Van Dijk’s contract expires in June and he’s always been fascinated by Milan and Italy. It’s complex, but it’s worth a try, and Cardinale seems to agree.

Then there is Gabriele Calvani. He’s Italian, 22, plays for Frosinone, and is expected to start San Siro on Sunday. The Diavolo are interested, just as they are keen on Sporting CP’s Gonçalo Inacio, whom Amorim has already coached and attempted to sign in the summer.

Milan will undoubtedly make some changes to their bench over the next 12 months, aiming to mix young players with experienced players. Filippo Terracciano will leave in January, Vladimirov needs to play, Hutchinson is on loan until June, and Jashari will have to reconsider his future.

Recent findings suggest that it’s certain that some Diawara-like players will arrive, i.e. promising prospects chosen through scouting and data. Markus Krösche – if he becomes the upcoming Head of Football, as is now almost certain – will have extensive powers in this regard.

The idea of ​​making the team more Italian is there, but we know how the market works, making it difficult to strategy. Not only that, but some Italians will soon leave Milan too. Above all, Christian Comotto and Francesco Camarda are heading out on loan.

In a recent development, the former seems destined for Daniele De Rossi’s Genoa, while it remains to be seen where and under what terms the altter will leave. A loan with an option to buy, leaving Milan free to control the future, probably. To a small Serie A team? Possibly, but a move abroad is possible too.

According to recent reports, belgium and the Netherlands are countries where strikers historically have more opportunities in teams that are younger, while Germany could be another destination. If he takes a flight north, don’t be surprised.

The stirring of what might yet be a great partnership between Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, although it will need to be, given some of the chaos that endures at Chelsea.

According to recent reports, this was a Premier League game played at a furious pace, and the two former Real Madrid team-mates in charge of the sides will not have seen much of the control all coaches seek. Xabi Alonso’s team eventually won with a goal from each of his attacking triumvirate of Rogers, Palmer and João Pedro – and at times it will have been painful for the new Chelsea manager.

That was chiefly the fault of Robert Sánchez, who was embraced afterwards by Alonso, having demonstrated just how damaging a shaky goalkeeper can be to any serious team. Álvaro Arbeloa’s Fulham had their moments – and the best ones were granted to them by Sánchez. At a club that is such a restless trader of footballers, it feels remarkable that Sánchez has endured for so long.

Alonso played down the significance of Sánchez’s errors, although he cannot seriously be considering sticking to his mantra of “relax and carry on”. That was, he remarked, his response to the first-half Sánchez mistake that let in Josh King’s shot for Fulham’s first goal. Sánchez could have done a lot better with Gonzalo García’s goal after the break.

Fulham have equalised against Chelsea thanks to Josh King's low strike 💥 pic.twitter.com/WCLKB7XqeE.

Gonzalo Garcia has scored on his Premier League debut after Robert Sanchez spilled Castagne's shot 🤯 pic.twitter.com/BmP6eqwkuN.

Chelsea have a lot of faith that Mike Penders, the 21-year-old Belgian on the bench for this game, will be their first-choice goalkeeper eventually. The situation seems rather more urgent and with Penders likely to feature against Luton Town on Thursday night in the Carabao Cup it would appear a big decision is looming for Alonso.

In terms of the Palmer-Rogers axis, this was very promising, although there was no doubting the senior figure in this. Palmer’s ball set João Pedro free in the first minute, the Brazilian lifting a well-judged nudge over Bernd Leno.

"A flying start under Xabi Alonso!" Chelsea lead against Fulham after just 31 seconds 🤯 pic.twitter.com/LrkYxOReFB.

It has been revealed that it was Palmer who was crucial to the second for Rogers, made by Maxence Lacroix on his debut. Palmer stroked in the third on 49 minutes with the easy confidence of a man in form.

A goal for Morgan Rogers on his Chelsea debut! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/hphe8y077v.

"Cole Palmer back to his best!"Palmer has scored to double Chelsea's lead! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/zo6e0Vdcgq.

“I am very happy for Cole,” Alonso noted. “I have really enjoyed seeing him play with the dynamism and the freedom and the responsibility... when Cole feels this way we have a better team and a better Cole.”.

Palmer makes it look very easy in this form, capable of switching the direction of play a beat before anyone else spots the opportunity. He and his old Manchester City academy friend Rogers came off before the end, Palmer having demonstrated some discomfort chasing a ball. Asked afterwards how ready he felt, Palmer responded in kind. “Did you not watch the game? I’m only joking, I’m ready... it was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot, but through the summer and since I’ve been back I’ve worked extra hard.”.

If there was an attacker to compare with him on the other side it was King, who looks even better. The 19-year-old was way ahead of Arbeloa’s two young Real Madrid imports. García toiled away and took his chance, but César Palacios struggled for any impact in a position tucked in on the left. Oscar Bobb and King gave Fulham some edge but the concern, as ever, will be where Fulham get their goals.

Arbeloa pushed his full-backs high and encouraged Sander Berge to drop deep to get on the ball in the first passing phase. The Norwegian delayed too long in challenging João Pedro for Chelsea’s third – backing off and allowing Palmer to overlap to receive the pass.

In a recent development, sánchez had not been the only concern for Chelsea. Back in the team, Levi Colwill misjudged a challenge on King in the first half and was relieved that the card was only yellow. Roméo Lavia took a wild swing at Calvin Bassey and was also booked. Moisés Caicedo was not fit to play. Enzo Fernández was on the bench and would come on in the second half to the kind of reception from opposition fans to which he will promptly become familiar.

There was a grin from the Argentine at those who berated him from the home stands when he returned at half-time. Fernández worked hard to transmit a general sense that the abuse did not land, although he will be relieved that the Chelsea fans were supportive. His future still feels very much in play.

According to recent reports, it was Palmer’s subtle ball through that gave João Pedro the chance with 32 seconds of the game played. The ball came forward immediately from Lacroix’s firm header from defence. The Frenchman delivered a very accomplished assist for Rogers’s first-half goal. Before that King had equalised. There was an exchange with Timothy Castagne, and King looked up just inside the box and decided to have a swing at it. Sánchez was close enough to grasp the ball and somehow failed to do so.

Sources indicate that sánchez would later push a Castagne shot in the direction of García, who stooped and nodded the ball over the goalkeeper after Palmer had scored Chelsea’s third. This second error was unfortunate, but it is the kind of thing that happens to a goalkeeper as erratic as the one for whom Chelsea’s hierarchy seem to have such patience.

“We concede goals in the first minute, the end of the first half and the beginning of the second half and there are not worse moments to concede. But we demonstrated character and personality and I am very proud of how my players responded. We deserved a little bit more but football is not about what you deserve, it is about what you take. If you lose against a team like Chelsea they [should] have to do a little bit more. For me, they are easy goals for them and mistakes we cannot make. We need to improve and be more ready in the first minute, that is for sure.

“We are on our way and we will keep improving. The first thing I want to see is a competitive team. We were tonight, we tried our best and tried to play our football against a team like Chelsea, which is not easy. I believe in them and I believe in young players. I think they have the energy and ambition I want and they fit in the way I play. Josh King is absolutely amazing. I am really happy with him. Gonzalo [Garcia] scored and Cesar [Palacios] did well. I think they need a bit more time but they are doing great and making an impact already.”.

"We need to help them, not to rely everything on them" Xabi Alonso speaking about Chelsea's 'special' front three 🔵 pic.twitter.com/JnSBoNexF4.

"Arsenal DON'T win the league if they have Ramsdale and not Raya" 🧤@Carra23 and @GNev2 think that upgrading the goalkeeper position could be the 'last piece' for Chelsea 🧩 pic.twitter.com/UBzMCFmxpp.

"You can see in his eyes, he's ready to prove people wrong""Best player on the pitch by a mile" 👏Morgan Rogers reacts to his debut and the performance of Cole Palmer pic.twitter.com/M7JKk1MQ8U.

"How ready are you?""Did you not watch the game?" 😅Cole Palmer states he is 'hungry' and ready to get back to his best! pic.twitter.com/xpg5zJl9k0.

In a recent development, “There were things to really like. On paper, that front three [for Chelsea] is sensational. It really is. It looked it in the game. I think Joao Pedro is fantastic. [Morgan] Rogers’ first game, what a start. But when you think of him, [Cole] Palmer and Pedro; that is as good as anything in the Premier League right now.

Recent findings suggest that “But I do think concerns defensively. They conceded a couple of goals and you look at the goalkeeper. They have to sort the goalkeeper issue out because it is going to come back to haunt them this season, as it did tonight.”.

“The attacking play, Cole Palmer was sensational. If you talk about Cole Palmer getting back to his best you have got a £120m-£125m player there. [Morgan] Rogers getting a goal. Those two being electric with Joao Pedro up front. The front three were brilliant tonight. One of the best things I have seen this weekend.

“They have added an experience player at centre-back, centre midfield and centre forward. I do not know if Emi Martinez is available or not but someone like that needs to come in at Chelsea, because that will undermine everything they do. The positives for Fulham came from the encouragement [Robert] Sanchez gave them with the goals. The goals were both mistakes. It is a problem.”.

According to recent reports, the final whistle is blown at Craven Cottage and Chelsea hold on to win 3-2 to give Xabi Alonso a win in his first game in charge. Alvaro Arbeloa’s first game as Fulham boss ends in defeat. An absorbing west London derby.

Garcia throws himself to the ground as Sessegnon sends in a cross but that is never going to be a penalty.

Industry observers note that will there be one more chance for Fulham to try and find an equaliser? Time is running out for the hosts.

Pedro has the ball in the back of the Fulham net but Quenda was offside in the build-up. A quick VAR check proves so.

There will be four added minutes.

Sources indicate that surely there is another goal in this one? It is a surprise there has not been since Garcia got a goal back for Fulham.

The latest booking of the game goes the way of Castagne, who cynically trips Colwill.

Sessegnon is played in down the left channel and flicks it past Acheampong inside the Chelsea penalty area. Sessegnon gets his shot away from a narrow angle and it is straight at Sanchez.

Sources indicate that palmer looks like he might have cramp in his calf and is going to be replaced by Estevao. Quenda also comes on for Chelsea, coming on for Rogers.

Fulham make an attacking alteration as Muniz replaces Robinson.

In a recent development, that is a huge, huge chance for Fulham to equalise. Robinson is played in behind the Chelsea defence with a long ball in behind and Sanchez is in no-man’s land out of his goal. Robinson just has to lift it over Sanchez from the edge of the box but his effort goes wide. Fulham should be on level terms.

Recent findings suggest that fulham fans think they are about to be awarded a free-kick right outside the box but instead the free-kick goes the other way. It was a clear dive from Bassey, who is rightly booked for simulation.

It has been revealed that james is the third Chelsea player into the book for cynically pulling King back. James then has the cheek to wag his finger at King, as if it was not a foul, yet it was a clear booking. James had to be careful there as some referees may not have taken too kindly to that.

Double change for Fulham as Kevin and Sessegnon are brought on.

That would have been a great goal from King. He has already scored once and is inches away from his second. He receives a pass on the turn from Robinson and drives towards the Chelsea box. He then cuts inside onto his right, beating Lacroix with ease, and nearly beats Sanchez at his near post but his shot goes inches wide.

This is a very open, end-to-end game and you would fully expect more goals in this one. I would be very surprised if this one ended 3-2. Both defences are looking leaky.

Fulham are going to make their substitution of the night as Charles comes on for his debut having signed from Southampton, replacing Bobb.

Enzo is being booed a lot by the home fans every time he touches the ball.

Chelsea are the first to turn to their bench. Enzo is coming on and is met by a lot of boos, mostly though from the home fans as the majority of the travelling Chelsea fans are applauding him. Chavarria is also on to make his Chelsea debut. Hato and Lavia head off.

There is a newly introduced rule being implemented. Hato takes far too long over a throw-in and Fulham are therefore awarded the throw-in instead.

When Palmer put Chelsea 3-1 up, the visitors looked in control of this match. Fast forward five minutes and the momentum has completely switched around. What an absorbing opening Monday night of the season!

According to recent reports, the Fulham debutant gives them life and this game is not over. Castagne is found making a run in behind and cuts back inside onto his left inside the Chelsea penalty area. His shot is straight at Sanchez, who can only parry it straight into the path of Garcia, who heads into the ground and the ball bounces over Sanchez into the Chelsea net. Another poor piece of goalkeeping from Sanchez.

Gonzalo Garcia has scored on his Premier League debut after Robert Sanchez spilled Castagne's shot 🤯 pic.twitter.com/BmP6eqwkuN.

All members of Chelsea’s starting front three have got on the scoresheet tonight and Palmer also has an assist to his name.

Chelsea come close to a fourth as Hato squares it for Rogers inside the Fulham box but Robinson nips in just in front to clear.

He came close to scoring moments ago and now he does get on the scoresheet. Pedro gets onto the end of a flicked-on header by Rogers near halfway and drives into the Fulham half. As he gets to the Fulham penalty area, he waits for the overlapping run of Palmer and times the pass just right. Palmer, from a narrow angle, puts it between Leno’s legs and into the far corner.

"Cole Palmer back to his best!"Palmer has scored to double Chelsea's lead! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/zo6e0Vdcgq.

Palmer does brilliantly down Chelsea’s right to skip past a number of defenders and moves into the Fulham penalty area. He opens up his body and curls one towards the far corner. He is adamant that there is a deflection but a goal kick is given. Replays show Palmer may have had a point.

We are back under way at Craven Cottage.

Nottingham Forest are ramping up their pursuit of Chelsea’s Liam Delap as Oliver Glasner eyes two major signings before the window closes.

Forest are in talks with Chelsea over a potential loan deal for the forward after he was made available at Stamford Bridge and not included in their opening-day squad against Fulham.

Negotiations are ongoing, but Delap fits the profile of striker Forest are prioritising and is a long-term target for both the club and Glasner from his spell at Crystal Palace.

According to recent reports, an absorbing first half at Craven Cottage is brought to a close and Chelsea take a 2-1 lead into the break. Pedro put them ahead inside the first minute before King equalised for Fulham. However Rogers, on his Chelsea debut, put the visitors back in front not long before half-time.

There will be two added minutes at the end of this first half.

According to recent reports, palmer, who has run the show for Chelsea in this first half, is inches away from putting the visitors 3-1 up. Both sides have been guilty of giving the ball away in dangerous areas and Fulham do so on this occasion. Palmer then curls an effort from the edge of the box but his shot goes just wide of the far post.

The British record transfer puts Chelsea back in front on his official debut. It stems from great play from centre-back Lacroix, who finds himself in an advanced position and receives a pass from Palmer on the right side of the box. Lacroix cuts it across to Rogers, who makes no mistake from 12 yards out. Assist and goal both coming from newly introduced signings.

Sources indicate that A goal for Morgan Rogers on his Chelsea debut! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/hphe8y077v.

Fulham fail to clear a cross from James into their box and Hato’s header falls at the feet of Lavia, whose shot from close range is saved by Leno.

Recent findings suggest that is Colwill lucky to still be on the pitch? The ball is played in behind the Chelsea defence and Colwill appeared to throw his arm across King but no foul is given. That could so easily have been given as a free-kick and a second yellow card.

Recent findings suggest that rogers drives towards the Fulham box and cuts inside onto his right foot. His effort is blocked by Cuenca before James’ first-time shot is straight at Leno.

Chelsea are inches from going back in front. It stems from great work from Palmer, who drives down Chelsea’s right. His cross from the right side of the box picks out Pedro near the penalty spot. The Brazilian volleys it first time but his effort goes just wide.

Fulham are on top at the moment and Chelsea are lucky shaky as they are under the cosh inside their own box. King is playing really well, finding pockets of space down Fulham’s right and looking a real threat.

Fulham are back on level terms but it is really poor goalkeeping from Sanchez. King, who had just threatened down Fulham’s right, receives a pass from Castagne on the right touchline and takes a touch into the Chelsea box. King then fires his shot away at the near post and gets plenty of power on it but there is no way Sanchez should be beaten. He is beaten and Fulham equalise. Good strike from King but terrible keeping from Sanchez.

Fulham have equalised against Chelsea thanks to Josh King's low strike 💥 pic.twitter.com/WCLKB7XqeE.

Chelsea haven’t spent all that money on Rogers for his defending, but Alonso won’t have liked the way he let Josh King to run past him to collect the ball and smash Fulham level. Rogers switched off there.

King does brilliantly to drive down Fulham’s right and flashes a dangerous ball across the six-yard box but none of his teammates are on hand to meet the cross.

Fulham are flirting with danger in and around their box and are a touch fortunate not to concede a second goal.

Down the other end, King is urged to shoot from outside the box and he obliges. It looks like it should be a fairly routine save for Sanchez but the Chelsea keeper looks uncomfortable and pushes it behind for a corner. The delivery comes to the near post and King, who lays it off the edge of the box. It comes to Palacios, who cannot guide his effort on target.

In a recent development, chelsea started this game well but have lost control and are asking for trouble. The latest example sees Sanchez take too long to clear and he accidentally allows the ball to go out before clearing to gift Fulham a corner. Bobb’s delivery is headed away at the near post by James.

It has been revealed that that is strong one-vs-one defending from Bassey. Palmer lifts the ball over the top to pick out the run of Pedro, who is dispossessed inside the Fulham box by Bassey.

Moments later, Lavia flies into a reckless challenge on Bassey and is booked. Lavia looks stunned at that decision but he is perhaps on the fortunate side that VAR did not advise the referee to have a further look at that on the screen. Lavia was out of control and could have easily been in more trouble. Two Chelsea players already into the book and were a little bit lucky.

Palmer had just one Premier League assist to his name throughout last season and has already matched that tally tonight on the opening weekend.

Colwill is in trouble. Could Chelsea go down to 10 men early? He loses possession poorly inside his own half and then resorts to hacking Bobb down with a nasty challenge. Was Colwill the last man and could Bobb have gone racing in on goal? Colwill is booked and is perhaps a touch fortunate, although what saved him is that you perhaps could not definitively say that it was a denial of a goal-scoring opportunity.

How do Alvaro Arbeloa and his Fulham side react now they are a goal down early?

According to recent reports, with their first attack of the Xabi Alonso era, Chelsea hit the front inside the opening minute of this west London derby. Lacroix’s header from halfway finds Palmer, who plays it into the path of Pedro. The Brazilian, fresh from signing a new deal at the club, takes it in his stride and, from inside the Fulham penalty area, lifts it over Leno and into the far corner. A fine finish from Pedro and Alonso has the perfect start.

"A flying start under Xabi Alonso!" Chelsea lead against Fulham after just 31 seconds 🤯 pic.twitter.com/LrkYxOReFB.

Could Joao Pedro be the man to finally lift the curse of the number nine shirt at Chelsea? Liam Delap tried and failed last season. Pedro has taken it this term and has started like a train with that early goal. Pedro has also been prolific in pre-season and has been widely tipped to be one of the Premier League’s top scorers.

Before we get going, we take a moment to remember the great Kevin Keegan, who managed Fulham in the late 1990s.

We are under way at Craven Cottage in the final game on this opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

Alvaro Arbeloa is out on the pitch for the first time in the Premier League. A friendly if not rapturous welcome from the home fans. He’s rolled his sleeves up and he’s ready to go - literally, his skinny fit jacket has sleeves rolled up tight. It looks quite uncomfortable.

It might be a new season and a new manager, but Chelsea are still doing their pre-match huddle. Fortunately, it was nowhere near the referee or the centre circle. It seemed to be captain Reece James doing all the talking.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at Craven Cottage and we are moments away from kick-off in this west London derby. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up tonight:.

No more excuses. No more jam tomorrow. It is time for Chelsea to fight for the Premier League title this season. Anything else should be deemed a disappointment.

This is Chelsea version 3.0 under BlueCo, who bought the club four years ago. First there was Todd Boehly’s trolley dash, then came Behdad Eghbali’s youth club. This summer the focus has been on being Premier League-ready.

It has been revealed that two former Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain teammates go head-to-head in the dugouts at Craven Cottage as Fulham host Chelsea in a west London derby to round out the opening weekend of the latest Premier League season. Alvaro Arbeloa and Xabi Alonso were teammates at Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain and both had stints as Real Madrid manager last season but have new homes in London. Arbeloa has replaced Marco Silva, who is now at Benfica, whilst Alonso is Liam Rosenior’s permanent replacement. This is the first time a manager’s Premier League debut has come against someone he also played alongside in the competition.

Recent findings suggest that “I know Alonso well because I have watched so many games of his teams,” Arbeloa said. “We have to be ready, and if we want to beat them we will have to play very well. I spoke to Xabi a few days ago. But not about football; both of our families are coming to London, and we are very good friends, until Monday night [tonight]. We will be there on the touchline, so close for 90 minutes, and we will give everything for our clubs. For those 90 minutes, we are not friends.”.

It has been revealed that arbeloa has gone back to his former club to add a couple of players in the shape of Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios. The opening weekend has not served Fulham well of late; they have won just one of their last six Premier League opening weekend fixtures. They concluded their pre-season with a 1-0 win over Stuttgart.

In a recent development, chelsea have been very active in the transfer market this summer, breaking the British transfer record to sign Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa as well as adding experience through the likes of Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck, whilst the likes of Marc Cucurella, Andrey Santos and Trevoh Chalobah have moved on. They finished off their pre-season with a 3-1 victory over Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge just over a week ago.

“We feel ready,” Alonso mentioned. “We have prepared the whole pre-season with some players from the first day, other ones coming later, but the desire, the ambition, the hunger to start the Premier League is already in the building each training [session] and we are looking forward to it.”.

Enzo Fernandez has been strongly linked with a move away this summer, with Manchester City’s interest well-known.

“Enzo is a Chelsea player,” Alonso added. “He is a top, top player. He is training really well since he started 10 days ago with the team, very integrated. We are happy with him and he is getting ready for Monday. He is training really well, good attitude and that is what we want. He is trying his best to prepare for the kick-off of the Premier League.”.

These sides finished on the same number of points (52) last season, with Chelsea finishing ahead on goal difference. It was one win apiece for each club in the two Premier League meetings last season. Nearly a year ago, Chelsea won 2-0 at Stamford Bridge whilst Fulham won 2-1 in this fixture at Craven Cottage back in January. Chelsea have won six of the past eight Premier League meetings at Craven Cottage.

#118172. Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

📅 25 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 21m • 📚 Deep Dive (4171 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

📅 25 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4171 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.
  • Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.
  • The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

“England’s No 1” was a frequent chant from the travelling Leeds fans and although it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice, he is loving life at his upcoming club.

Trafford produced a number of fine saves and goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable Carabao Cup second-round victory for Leeds, who also won here in the league on Saturday.

Dan James has put Leeds ahead against Nottingham Forest 💥 pic.twitter.com/BdiYMXFJ5h.

Leeds manager Daniel Farke said: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

“I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

“He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”.

Forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

According to recent reports, forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a fresh right wing-back before the deadline.

Sources indicate that newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

Glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He stated: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

“For nine months last season we were fighting relegation, so the players know it is going to take a lot of work. I know exactly what we have to change and that is what we will do.

Industry observers note that “We are responsible and made so many mistakes. Maybe we needed this result. At the moment we are far away from what we want but we will get there.”.

This was a more open game than the attritional encounter from last weekend, as Trafford was forced into a fine early save to prevent Ola Aina’s cross from arcing into the top corner.

Yet both teams were frequently making mistakes and providing masterclasses in how to misplace passes, frustrating their respective managers in the technical area.

Recent findings suggest that the most impressive moment of the first-half came from Leeds centre-back Joe Rodon, racing back into position to deny Chris Wood from close range. Rodon celebrated the tackle as if it were a 30-yard screamer.

It was always likely to be a mistake which proved the pivotal moment, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s poor header cost the home team in the 50th minute.

Kalimuendo’s error presented Sean Longstaff with space to run into and his pass found James, who beat Matz Sels with a clinical finish.

“Can we play you every week?” was the inevitable chant from the travelling Leeds supporters.

Forest’s fans were becoming twitchy and Trafford produced another save to frustrate Wood from eight yards after a break down the right from Kalimuendo.

Glasner responded by making a quadruple substitution on the hour, yet Leeds remained dangerous and added a second goal 15 minutes from time when Justin bundled home after a goalmouth scramble.

In a recent development, ethan Ampadu's long throw causes CHAOS in the Forest box as Leeds go 2-0 up! pic.twitter.com/CtGDDIaRNp.

You can catch the draw for the next stage of the League Cup on Sky Sports Main Event tomorrow night after the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record deal worth £45m for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

Delap has been deemed surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, and while the clubs were in talks over an initial loan deal, they have now struck a permanent agreement for the striker.

According to recent reports, the 23-year-old​ only signed for Chelsea in a £30m deal from Ipswich Town 12 months ago​ ​and is scheduled for a medical on Wednesday​. He will become Forest’s most expensive signing with the deal eclipsing the £37.5m they paid for Omari Hutchinson last summer.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a newly introduced forward and Delap was a long-term target for the Austrian since his time as Crystal Palace head coach.

Delap held talks with Forest last year over a potential move, and was also understood to have spoken with Glasner while he was at Palace.

According to recent reports, speaking to ITV after the win, Rodon remarked: “I thought we were a bit sharper going forward, maybe a bit naive in the first half. I thought we had a lot of good chances maybe could have scored a couple of goals but we know it’s a difficult place to come and overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game.”.

In a recent development, of his last-ditch tackle in the first half, he added: “We love it, as defenders it’s as good as a goal. I’m delighted, [keeping] clean sheets is my job and overall I got it right in the end.”.

"There's a healthy arrogance about Leeds""Farke has gone from strength to strength"Izzy Christiansen and Jobi McAnuff praise the impact of Daniel Farke at Leeds 📈 pic.twitter.com/fgzLWRk3U2.

"It's a bit soon to say Wembley!" 😅James Justin and Dan James react to Leeds progressing into round three of the Carabao Cup 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/m81C6eJT7C.

Aug 30: Leeds United vs BrentfordSep 5: Brighton and Hove Albion vs Leeds UnitedSep 14: Leeds United vs Newcastle UnitedSep 19: Leeds United vs Crystal PalaceOct 10: Arsenal vs Leeds United.

Aug 29: Liverpool vs Nottingham ForestSep 5: Nottingham Forest vs Tottenham HotspurSep 12: Aston Villa vs Nottingham ForestSep 19: Nottingham Forest vs CoventryOct 11: Crystal Palace vs Nottingham Forest.

A tough night for the home teams...

Cardiff City 1 Norwich 2Doncaster Rovers 1 Middlesbrough 3Barnsley 3 Crewe Alexandra 2Blackburn Rovers 1 Sheffield United 2Blackpool 1 Lincoln City 4Cambridge United 0 Millwall 1Fleetwood Town 4 Shrewsbury Town 0Ipswich Town 3 Leicester City 1Plymouth 2 Coventry City 4Sheffield Wednesday 0 Wolverhampton Wanderers 2Southampton 1 West Ham United 4Stevenage Town 0 Reading 3Stoke City 1 Hull City 1 (4-5 pens)Walsall 0 Leyton Orient 0 (5-6 pens)Watford 1 Peterborough United 5Birmingham City 1 Brentford 6Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2.

It has been revealed that and that is it. Two home defeats by Leeds in less than 80 hours for Forest. Glasner will have much to ponder with a daunting trip to Anfield coming up on Saturday. All smiles for Farke’s side.

According to recent reports, A look at a third for Leeds. Aaronson drives forward before setting Wilson who in turn lays on a first-time pass to Calvert-Lewin. The forward attempts to take his shot first time but can’t get the requisite power on the ball to beat Sels.

A pitch invader makes a brief appearance on the turf but is swiftly ushered away.

There is a late chance for Forest. Hutchinson’s cross is helped on by Dominguez but that touch inadvertently takes the ball away from Ndoye at the back post.

Forest fans are filing out of the exits and who can blame them?

There will be six minutes of added time.

That just about sums up Forest’s night. Dominguez stands over a free-kick from a dangerous area and, with the box loaded with their most imposing aerial threats, the midfielder sends the ball well over their heads and out for a goal-kick. So poor.

According to recent reports, calvert-Lewin is now on for Nmecha. Not really the striker Forest defenders would want to see at this stage of the game.

Another set-piece, this time a Stach corner, is barely dealt with by Forest.

There’s a shout for a handball at the other end as Ndoye spears a cross into the body of Elvedi, but the referee rightly waves the appeals away.

The “oles” ring out from the away end as Leeds string a series of passes together in the corner right in front of it. Forest are looking rather helpless here.

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2 (Justin) Ampadu launches a throw-in from the right but has to reload as the referee notices some pushing in the box. His next attempt is far too loopy but causes Forest all sorts of trouble, bouncing and bobbling, and coming all the way through a thicket of limbs to Nmecha at the far post. The resulting free-kick lands to Amapadu himself in the box, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

Stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

The substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

Okafor shows off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”.

This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

Both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

In a recent development, should the scores remain level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. There’s still a half to play of course, but Forest’s League Cup shoot-out record should be a source of confidence having won seven from eight.

Leeds have only won four from 10.

And, quite aptly, the referee blows up at three seconds past 45 minutes. Certainly not a half for the books.

In a recent development, another half-chance for Forest! Milenkovic lands on a second ball off a deep free-kick but he cannot keep his strike down. A classic centre-half’s effort if you will.

Just as I type that Forest threaten with a ball over the top, but Justin nips in to take the ball away from Wood.

Recent findings suggest that another decent opening for Leeds after a Forest turnover. Nmecha strides through the middle but Milenkovic is in position to ensure his run comes to nothing.

Recent findings suggest that what a tackle! Kalimuendo bursts through the middle after Leeds cede possession in a dangerous position. It’s then Okafor’s turn to put in a dangerous cross from the left, but Nmecha cannot get to it.

It has been revealed that tanaka becomes the first man to go into the book. The ball gets away from him and Jesus puts body between man and ball smartly to win the foul.

Sources indicate that tanaka is now dropping into the back line to allow Leeds’ defenders the licence to get wider and higher. Forest will need to be wary of their opponents’ numerical advantage down the flanks.

It has been revealed that the game has reached something of a holding pattern as both sides resolve to slow things down, at least temporarily. Forest have settled into a slightly deeper block.

Industry observers note that sensing an opportunity, Ampadu spins in a glorious through-ball between centre-back and full-back for James to gallop on to. He hits the by-line and cuts back to Longstaff, but the midfielder can’t beat Sels. A good chance that probably should have been converted.

According to recent reports, both sides have physical, quick out-balls, which has made for a frenetic encounter thus far. James rasps in another fierce cross from the right after another sweeping Leeds move, but Nmecha cannot get there and Tanaka fires well over on the follow-up.

Aina’s throw-in, this time from the left, is flicked on to Jesus at the back post and while the forward is able to direct the ball goalwards there is Justin on the line to clear the ball to safety.

Wonderful touch there early in the game from none other than Oliver Glasner.

Forest’s head coach perfectly trapped a high ball as it landed towards him in the technical area.
